text:
Montreal hosts San Jose tonight with the better underlying numbers. At five on five, MTL has taken 55% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) in its games, against 45% for SJS. The Sharks give up 3.8 expected goals per 60 minutes, the Canadiens 3.4, and the model projects 3.39 expected goals for MTL tonight to 3.0 for SJS. On special teams, MTL's penalty kill allows 0.81 expected goals a game to SJS's 1.05, though the Canadiens take 5.4 penalties a game, which keeps handing opponents power plays. SJS is also on the second night of a back-to-back after a 1-3 loss in Toronto, while MTL has had two days off.

In goal, projected starters Alex Nedeljkovic (SJS) and Jacob Fowler (MTL) both come in positive this season in goals saved above expected, which counts the goals a goalie prevented beyond what the quality of shots faced would predict: +4.22 for Nedeljkovic over 3 games, +1.99 for Fowler over 4. Last season they split the other way, Nedeljkovic at -2.06 over 40 games and Fowler at +5.98 over 17. Nedeljkovic gets the nod over Yaroslav Askarov, who has made 6 of San Jose's 9 starts.

Recent form favors MTL as well. The Canadiens are 3-2-0 in their last five and had more expected goals in four of them. The Sharks are 1-3-1 and out-chanced opponents once. Montreal is without Ivan Demidov (lower body), though Mike Matheson could return. Watch Macklin Celebrini, given a 43% chance to score and 84% to get a point, and Cole Caufield, also at 43% to score.
